---
title: "Reproduce"
subtitle: "The pipeline, its configuration, and what it will not do for you"
---

Everything on this site is generated by a five-stage pipeline from four inputs:
a CAD drawing, a DEM, a service boundary, and a population total.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Manish-Bilore/wdn-digital-twin
cd wdn-digital-twin
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
apt install gdal-bin                     # ogr2ogr, for DWG/DXF

python pipeline/run_all.py -c config.yml
python pipeline/scripts/05_export_web.py -o outputs -s site
quarto render site
```

| Stage | Does |
|---|---|
| `01_ingest_cad` | layer selection, georeferencing, annotation parsing |
| `02_build_model` | topology repair, elevations, demand, diameters, EPANET solve |
| `03_place_sensors` | K-means districts, overlay filter, figures |
| `04_emit_ontology` | ABox emission, TBox merge, validation |
| `05_export_web` | GeoJSON, graph and charts for this site |

Every stage writes to `outputs/` and can be re-run alone.

## Swapping in another network

The pipeline is not IIT Bombay specific. Point `config.yml` at your own DWG,
DEM and boundary, set the population, and it runs. Attribute columns are matched
fuzzily, the CRS can be derived from the boundary layer, and the DEM is
reprojected on the fly.

Two settings will need attention on any new site: `cad.extent_filter`, if the
sheet carries more than one block of linework, and `topology.max_bridge_gap_m`,
which controls how aggressively disconnected branches are reconnected. Both
print diagnostics on every run.

## What the pipeline will not do

It will not tell you the drawing is wrong. If a main is missing from the CAD it
is missing from the model, and no amount of topology repair invents it.

It will not survey your network. The georeference is solved against a boundary
polygon, to something like 10–30 m. Supply real control points if you need
better, and the pipeline will use them.

It will not validate demand. The area-based method assumes consumption tracks
plan area, which is wrong for a campus where a hostel block and a playing field
occupy similar footprints. Per-building occupancy would be a genuine improvement
and the allocation module has a hook for it.
